english.title: Dealer fail to exhibit / keep exhibited an approved notice as to hallmarks
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person engaged in the business of making, supplying, selling or exchanging articles of precious metal or in other dealings in such articles, failed to

(A)_[exhibit]_
(B)_[keep exhibited]_

in a conspicuous position in a part of your premises to which those with whom you dealt were commonly admitted, a notice in terms approved and in a form supplied by the British Hallmarking Council describing such approved hallmarks and including such explanatory matters as were thought fit by the Council
english.legislation: Contrary to section 11(1) of and Schedule 3 to the Hallmarking Act 1973.

english.notes:
(i) Section 10 of the Hallmarking Act 1973 allows the court, following conviction, to order any article the subject of the proceedings to be delivered to an assay office who, (subject to the order), may exercise the like powers under this Act in relation to the article as if it had been submitted to them for hallmarking.
(ii) The time limit on prosecutions is three years from the commission of the offence or one year from its discovery by the prosecutor whichever is the earlier (Para. 2 of Schedule 3).

Indictment : Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.
